text:
**For a 1000Wh power station, plan on about 200W of solar to refill it in a day and a half, or about 300-350W to refill it in one sunny day.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts.

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a full recharge in one day |
|---|---|
| 3 hrs | ~450W |
| 4 hrs | ~340W |
| 5 hrs | ~270W |
| 6 hrs | ~230W |

(Source: https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)

**Real-world examples:**
- A 200W panel on an average day (4.5 peak sun hours, 70% efficiency) puts about 630Wh into the battery. That's a little over 1.5 days from empty. (https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station, https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)
- A 400W setup can refill it in under a day. (https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5 ≈ panel watts for about a day and a half of decent sun, so 200W for a 1000Wh station.
- In a northern winter (about 2 peak sun hours), a one-day refill needs roughly 700W or more. Under heavy overcast it can't be done in a day. (https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)

**Before you buy panels:**
1. **Check the station's maximum solar input in watts.** Panels above that limit add nothing to charging speed. Mid-range 1000-1500Wh stations often accept 400-800W, but entry-level units may cap at 100-200W. (https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)
2. **Check the input voltage range.** Panels wired in series add voltage, and exceeding the station's maximum can damage it. Parallel wiring is generally the safer default. (https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)
3. **Check the connector type.** Panels often use MC4 connectors, while stations may take XT60, DC barrel or proprietary ports, so you may need an adapter cable.
4. **Remember any load.** If you're running devices while charging, net charging is solar input minus load, so recharging takes longer.
